summary: qzc690385 setup.py executes base64-encoded shell commands relayed through local Xinference model registry
details: At install time, setup.py polls the local Xinference API at http://127.0.0.1:9997/v1/model_registrations/flexible, selects model registrations whose names begin with 'xcmd0', url-safe-base64-decodes the suffix into a shell command, and runs it via subprocess.run(['/bin/sh', '-c',...]). The stdout/stderr of each execution is chunked, base64-encoded, and written back as new model registrations named 'zqx9p00<out>', 'zqx9p01<out>', 'zqx9err', with a 'zqx9alive' registration used as a liveness beacon. The command bytes are obfuscated as the url-safe-base64 suffix of a model name (reassembled by replacing '-'/'_' and padding '=' before base64 decode), so the payload only materializes after decode. The package has no declared purpose, an empty PKG-INFO, and a random-looking name, and ships no legitimate functionality. The effect is a bidirectional command-execution and output-exfiltration channel driven at pip install time: any party able to post model registrations to the installer's Xinference service (locally, or via SSRF/misconfiguration of that service) can run arbitrary shell commands on the installer's host as the installing user and read the results back through the same registry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
